Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The tight market split between 30°C and 31°C captures genuine uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and any timing shifts in cloud cover or precipitation, with updated model runs and local observations expected to narrow the outcome before resolution. Historical August averages near 29–30°C provide context for why traders view outcomes above 32°C as low-probability under current patterns.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent heatwave conditions driven by Typhoon Dolphin’s subsiding air are sustaining elevated temperatures into mid-August, but increasing convective activity and cloud cover are expected to moderate peaks on August 13.** Official Hong Kong Observatory guidance and ensemble models point to daytime maxima centered on 32–33°C under sunny periods or partly cloudy skies, with isolated thundery showers possible that could limit further warming. Historical August climatology shows mean maxima near 31–32°C, yet the current synoptic setup—warm southeasterly flow and residual subsidence—supports brief excursions to 34°C in urban or inland areas if skies remain clearer longer than anticipated.  

The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 32–33°C reflects this narrow uncertainty band: modest differences in timing of cloud build-up, shower coverage, or boundary-layer mixing can easily shift the official daily maximum by 1°C. Forecasters note that any organized convection later in the day would favor the lower end of the range, while prolonged sunshine would push toward 34°C; longer-range seasonal outlooks already indicate normal-to-above-normal warmth overall. Traders are therefore weighting the balance between persistent heat and the first signs of relief from increasing moisture and instability.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction runs from Météo-France and ECMWF show a strong high-pressure ridge advecting warm subtropical air over northern France, positioning Paris for a daily maximum near 38°C on August 13. Ensemble guidance clusters tightly around 37–39°C, with limited spread reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and urban heat-island effects at the official Paris-Le Bourget station. This warm anomaly aligns with the ongoing positive temperature trend observed across western Europe this summer and exceeds the long-term August climatology of 24–26°C. Traders have therefore assigned the highest implied probability to 38°C, while still pricing modest risk of a 1°C forecast adjustment from the final 12–24-hour model updates.
